Inflation's getting worse, new government data show consumer prices in the U.S. were higher in September and the same time a year earlier.
Tens of millions of people on Social Security meanwhile will see their monthly benefits go up next year by around $75 a month to help keep pace with the higher cost of living.
And Pierre Scott Horsley has more.
Investors think the somewhat hotter than expected cost of living report makes it more likely the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates.
When policymakers meet later this month, consumer prices in September were up 3.7 percent from a year ago.
That's a sharper annual increase than the previous month.
The U.S. war with Iran has triggered a big run-up in energy prices.
Rents and restaurant prices are climbing as well.
Average wages are not keeping pace with the higher cost of living.
People who depend on Social Security, however, will get a cost of living adjustment of 3.6 percent beginning in the new year.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
Netflix plans to cut 6 percent of its workforce.
And Pierre's Mandalit Del Barco reports it's the biggest round of layoffs in four years.
Netflix staffers around the world got the news today that a thousand of them are losing their jobs.
In an email memo to employees, co-CEO's Greg Peters and Ted Sarandos wrote that most of the cuts would be in Netflix's product, tech, legal and HR teams.
With increased competition and slower growth, the streamer has been trying to get subscribers to spend more time on its platform by adding live sports and events, video podcasts and shows by YouTube creators.
Netflix joins other tech and media companies with recent layoffs, including Amazon and Disney.
And the new Skydance merger of Paramount and Warner Brothers is expected to result in job cuts soon.
Mandalit Del Barco, NPR News, Los Angeles.
President Trump's spending the final weeks of the midterm campaign season visiting primarily GOP strongholds.
Today, he's scheduled to stump a Republican candidate in Arizona and Montana.
National polls continue to show low public approval ratings for Trump, including over his handling of the economy.
A federal appeals court is considering arguments over whether National Guard members deployed to Washington, D.C. more than 14 months ago should leave.
President Trump deployed the guard as part of what he described as a crime-fighting operation in the overwhelmingly Democratic city.
Deputy Assistant Attorney General Eric MacArthur argued for the Justice Department today.
More to the point, however, the deployments are also lawful.
As a unanimous panel of this court concluded in granting a state pending appeal, the president likely acted within his broad authority under both the D.C. militia code and 32 U.S.C. Section 502 F.
But D.C.'s attorney generals argue the president did not have the authority to deploy the National Guard to Washington, D.C.
This is NPR News.
A.I. development is mostly associated in our minds with replacing white-collar jobs and even destroying humanity.
But in India, A.I. is being developed to replace industrial jobs.
And Piersdia Hadid reports factory workers are training their own replacements.
In a textile factory in the southern Indian town of Karur, women pack aprons into plastic packaging and record their every hand movement through a GoPro fastened on a headset.
That footage is called egocentric data.
Developers need millions of hours of it to train A.I. robots.
Even as experts say, India is emerging as a key place to record egocentric data, they say the development of A.I. robots will likely be deployed in countries where labor is more expensive and power is cheaper.
They say these women in factory jobs might be saved by the fact that their labor is cheap.
Most are paid around $100 a month, and power here is considered expensive for now.
Dear Hadid, NPR News, Karur, Tamil Nadu, India.
Republican Congresswoman Nancy Mace's ex-fiance and two of his business associates are charged with sex crimes and voyeurism in South Carolina.
According to sworn statements from agents with the state law enforcement division, John Douglas Osborne is accused of crimes against a 23-year-old woman who is intoxicated while Mace's former fiancé Patrick Bryan and Eric Bernard Bowman allegedly watched.
Actor and comedian Russell Brand is on trial in Britain for sexual assault and rape. Brand has denied the allegations.
I'm Lakshmi Singh, NPR News, in Washington.
